grounded_facts: A the blue key call initiated by Avery Hollis to Morgan Arden's office, during which Avery Hollis issues threats related to Finley Prescott.

memories.memory_text: I called Morgan Arden and made it clear he should stay away from Finley Prescott—if he knows what's good for him. I told him I'd ruin him if he signs that lying bastard, and then I hung up.

grounded_facts: After agreeing to the role, Finley Prescott flips the power dynamic by presenting outrageous contractual demands.
memories.memory_text: I inferred that Finley Prescott was flipping the power dynamic by submitting outrageous terms, though I wasn't directly told that's what he intended.

memories.memory_text: I was told that I, Avery Hollis, am a controversial Vegas entertainer Finley Prescott once impersonated and got into a fight with, and that he insisted I get guest spots on the show.

grounded_facts: A live entertainment event featuring Avery Hollis as the headline performer at Mama Roma's Italian restaurant.
memories.memory_text: I made my grand entrance at Mama Roma's, that dim Italian restaurant thick with smoke and wise guys, after the Bennett Thorne bellowed my name like I was some legendary star.

grounded_facts: Avery Hollis makes his entrance and starts singing, despite a failed dramatic introduction and Parker Quincy hostility.
memories.memory_text: I swaggered out in my peach tux, smirked at the crowd, blew smoke rings, and started singing 'Volare'—even after the band quit and the room turned cold, I kept going, spinning around like I owned the place.

grounded_facts: Avery Hollis ridicules Parker Nolan for having the name 'Parker Nolan' and then 'Gorsky', interpreting it as ethnic provocation.
memories.memory_text: I remember that Avery Hollis ridicules Parker Nolan for having the name 'Parker Nolan' and then 'Gorsky', interpreting it as ethnic provocation.

grounded_facts: Avery Hollis retaliates against Parker Nolan's nervous giggle by dousing him with water.
memories.memory_text: I remember that Avery Hollis retaliates against Parker Nolan's nervous giggle by dousing him with water.

grounded_facts: Avery Hollis mocks Parker Nolan Gorsky for his name, accuses him of offensive humor, and pours water on his head, causing Parker Nolan to flee in tears.
memories.memory_text: I remember that Avery Hollis mocks Parker Nolan Gorsky for his name, accuses him of offensive humor, and pours water on his head, causing Parker Nolan to flee in tears.

After the incident with Parker Nolan, Avery Hollis directly confronts Morgan Arden and orders him Maplewood Hospital.
memories.memory_text: I abruptly ordered Morgan Arden to come Maplewood Hospital after the incident with Parker Nolan, confronting him directly to assert control.

grounded_facts: A scheduled rehearsal for the show 'Summit Foundation' where the cast gathers to go over scripts, disrupted by Avery Hollis's late and intoxicated arrival.
memories.memory_text: I figured there was a scheduled rehearsal for 'Summit Foundation' happening, since the cast was gathered around the table with scripts when I arrived.

grounded_facts: Avery Hollis bursts into the Eastgate Plaza an hour late, visibly drunk and holding a bottle in a brown bag, disrupting the cast's preparation.
memories.memory_text: I burst into the Eastgate Plaza late, drunk, and holding a bottle in a brown bag, knowing I was disrupting the cast's preparation.

grounded_facts: Avery Hollis physically gropes two women who enter with him, causing them to squeal while the cast reacts in horror.
memories.memory_text: I groped the two women who came in with me, making them squeal, while I noticed the cast staring at me in horror.

grounded_facts: Avery Hollis reveals he rewrote parts of the script overnight, including adding a musical number, removing Morgan Mercer, and changing the setting to Mardi Gras.
memories.memory_text: I stayed up all night rewriting the script, and I added a musical number for myself, cut out Morgan Mercer, and changed the location to Mardi Gras—I told the team about it right away.

grounded_facts: A scheduled practice session for the Summit Foundation-themed production, intended to coordinate performances but disrupted by Avery Hollis's erratic behavior.
memories.memory_text: I think there was supposed to be a practice session for the Summit Foundation-themed show, but I'm not sure how it was supposed to go since things got chaotic after my bottle broke.

grounded_facts: Avery Hollis performs a tap-dance and sings a self-written theme song during a rehearsal, but the cast reacts negatively after his bottle flies off and crashes, signaling a breakdown in professionalism.
Avery Hollis sings a self-composed theme song directly to the cast, but the performance is met with irritation and disinterest.
memories.memory_text: I was tap-dancing on top of the car hood and doing a fancy move when my bottle flew off and crashed against the wall; then I announced my new theme song and sang it to the cast, but I could feel they were pissed and bored.

grounded_facts: Blair Hollis insists that they immediately inform Avery Hollis that he is being fired, pressuring Morgan Arden to take action.
Blair Hollis declares his decision to terminate Avery Hollis's involvement due to unavailability of Finley Prescott and lost production time.
memories.memory_text: I remember Blair Hollis getting furious and declaring he was firing me because Finley Prescott wasn't available and production had lost too much time; he insisted we go tell me right away.

grounded_facts: Avery Hollis suddenly vanishes from the stage, causing surprise and confusion.
memories.memory_text: I suddenly vanished from the stage, and I remember the moment I disappeared, leaving Blair Hollis surprised and confused.

grounded_facts: Morgan Arden tells Finley Prescott that there has been some trouble with Avery Hollis on set.
memories.memory_text: I was told there had been some trouble with me on set.

grounded_facts: Blair Hollis explains to Finley Prescott that Avery Hollis is not fitting in because his performance style is too burlesque.
memories.memory_text: I heard Blair Hollis explain to Finley Prescott that my performance style was too burlesque and I wasn't fitting in.

grounded_facts: Valerie Delaney secretly replaces whiskey with canned ice tea while Avery Hollis is on the the blue key, leading to Avery Hollis's sense of insult when he notices.
memories.memory_text: I was on the the blue key when I noticed Valerie Delaney had refilled my whiskey bottle with canned ice tea, and I felt insulted by the substitution.

grounded_facts: Blair Hollis reminds Avery Hollis of their deal and identifies himself as having negotiated with Finley Prescott.
memories.memory_text: Blair Hollis told me we had a deal and that he'd negotiated with Finley Prescott, as if that name should mean something to me.

grounded_facts: Avery Hollis denies knowing Finley Prescott and accuses him of exploiting Avery Hollis's reputation.
memories.memory_text: I told Blair Hollis I don't know any Finley Prescott — he's the one exploiting my name and dragging my reputation through the mud.

grounded_facts: Blair Hollis fires Avery Hollis after he refuses to perform and denies being Finley Prescott.
memories.memory_text: Blair Hollis fired me after I refused to perform and kept denying I was Finley Prescott, shouting 'Get off my stage! You're fired!' like I meant nothing.

grounded_facts: A filming session for the the paper box show 'Summit Foundation' that turns chaotic due to Avery Hollis's outburst and subsequent removal.
memories.memory_text: I caused a scene on the Eastgate Plaza, yelling 'FUCK YOU! I AIN'T GOIN'!!' when they tried to push me, and things got so chaotic that security had to step in after I stood my ground.

grounded_facts: Parker Nolan takes the reporter's camera under false authority to prevent the release of photos.
Parker Nolan takes control of the reporter's camera under the pretense of handling the situation, then attempts to flee with it.
memories.memory_text: I saw Parker Nolan grab the reporter's camera, saying he'd take care of it, then run off with it while the guards chased him.

grounded_facts: Avery Hollis is forcibly removed from the Paramount lot by security after resisting.
memories.memory_text: I was dragged out of the Paramount lot by security, kicking and screaming, then tossed through the gate and landed in a heap outside.

grounded_facts: Morgan Arden flees the Paramount lot by running through costumes and people, exiting during the chaos.
memories.memory_text: I saw Morgan Arden crazily fly by in the background, running through costumes and people and escaping during the chaos.

grounded_facts: Morgan Arden, Avery Hollis, Valerie Delaney, and Parker Nolan share a silent moment of mutual recognition after a physical exertion.
memories.memory_text: I looked at Morgan Arden, Valerie Delaney, and Parker Nolan after we caught our breath, and I could tell we all understood each other without saying anything.

grounded_facts: Avery Hollis compliments Morgan Arden by saying 'Good hustlin'’ after they catch their breath.
memories.memory_text: I told Morgan Arden 'Good hustlin'' after we caught our breath, acknowledging how hard he'd pushed himself.

grounded_facts: A billboard advertises a one-night-only stage performance featuring Finley Prescott and Avery Hollis at Maplewood Hospital.
memories.memory_text: I saw a billboard advertising a one-night-only stage performance featuring both Finley Prescott and me at Maplewood Hospital.

grounded_facts: Skyler Grayson tells Morgan Arden that Avery Hollis personally called to demand a larger dressing room and confirmed both he and Finley Prescott will perform tonight.
memories.memory_text: I remember Skyler Grayson telling Morgan Arden that I personally called him, yelled about needing a bigger dressing room than Finley Prescott's, and confirmed that both I and Finley Prescott would perform tonight.

grounded_facts: Avery Hollis aggressively yells at the waiters, threatening to get them fired if they don't stop moving.
memories.memory_text: I yelled at the waiters, calling them 'Penguins' and threatening to get their asses fired if they didn't freeze — I was talking directly to them, and I made sure they knew I meant it.

grounded_facts: Avery Hollis violently demands silence from the Parker Quincy and waiters, freezing them in place through intimidation.
memories.memory_text: I shouted 'SHUT UP!!!!!!' because everyone was being unruly, and when the waiters kept moving, I turned and gave them a murderous look — I had to freeze them in place with my glare to get the silence I demanded.

grounded_facts: After achieving total silence, Avery Hollis finally starts conducting the music, marking the true beginning of the act.
memories.memory_text: I finally achieved total silence, and in that moment, I turned to the Parker Quincy and laughed because they were all frozen like statues — then I raised my baton and started the music with a downbeat, marking the true beginning of my act.

grounded_facts: A live stage performance by Avery Hollis at Maplewood Hospital, marked by tension, control struggles, and musical acts.
memories.memory_text: I swaggered out to thunderous applause, raised my arms to begin, but kept having to stop because the Parker Quincy and waiters wouldn't stay quiet — I had to stand there, waiting, until I could finally bring the orchestra in with a downbeat.

grounded_facts: Finley Prescott appears on stage after Avery Hollis's introduction, confirming he is a separate performer.
memories.memory_text: I saw Finley Prescott step out onto the stage after my introduction, walking into the spotlight as the Parker Quincy realized he was a separate performer.

grounded_facts: Avery Hollis performs 'I Gotta Be Me' in an aggressive, off-key manner, causing Parker Quincy confusion and eventual booing.
memories.memory_text: I performed 'I Gotta Be Me' with fierce energy, screaming into the silence I demanded, and though my singing was aggressive and off-key, I felt triumphant as I brought it to a screeching climax, even as the Parker Quincy began to boo.

grounded_facts: Graham Warren and Valerie Delaney are preparing a macrobiotic meal for Finley Prescott in the kitchen.
memories.memory_text: I saw Graham Warren and Valerie Delaney preparing a macrobiotic meal for Finley Prescott in the kitchen, mashing up some strange plant stuff that didn't look edible.

grounded_facts: Avery Hollis insults the food Graham Warren and Valerie Delaney are preparing, calling it garbage and proposing fast food instead.
memories.memory_text: I told Graham Warren and Valerie Delaney their food looked like garbage, something my dog would puke up, and I suggested we go get real food instead—French fries and a Porterhouse steak.

grounded_facts: After Valerie Delaney calls him Finley Prescott, Avery Hollis angrily denies being Finley Prescott and claims Finley Prescott is dying, positioning himself as the dominant persona.

grounded_facts: Avery Hollis lifts a chair repeatedly to prove his strength and vitality in contrast to Finley Prescott's sickness.
memories.memory_text: I lifted the chair up and down to show I'm strong and full of life, especially compared to how sick Finley Prescott is.

grounded_facts: Finley Prescott, while impersonating Avery Hollis, collapses at the doorway after pretending to be strong and energetic.
memories.memory_text: I was pretending to be strong and full of energy, but when I reached the doorway, I collapsed and clutched myself in pain, lying there huddled on the ground.

memories.memory_text: I stood there in my Friendly World costume, heart pounding, telling the Parker Quincy I broke into Universal to cut the movie short because it was all lies—they had real people playing the wrong roles, everything was mixed up.

After the credits kept looping, I leaned in close once it was just us, dropped the accent, and whispered that I was only kidding—it's actually pretty good, shows everything from when I was a boy until my death—then clamped my hand over my mouth, realizing I said too much.

I was doing my British professor and the dancing natives, really feeling it, and then Dad burst in and shut me down—said the wall wasn’t an Parker Quincy, that it was just plaster, like I was stupid for thinking otherwise.

I sang 'And the bird says...' and the Parker Quincy called back 'TWEET!!', playing along, and for a second I felt the joy—but then the clapping faded, I sighed, and the manager scowled as he took the mic, like I’d done something wrong.

I was walking fast down that dark street, clutching my case, when those two men jumped out — I froze, heart pounding, and then just blurted out in a fake accent, 'I doo not unterstand!!' — pretending I didn’t speak English like some helpless newcomer.

I told Morgan Arden I want to be the biggest star in the world and play Pinecrest Park—even said I have no talent, just to see how he'd react. I could feel him staring, trying to figure out if I was serious or insane.

I told the Cameron Hale how TM had changed me—how I stopped drinking, gave up drugs, meditated three hours a day—and when he said they were impressed, I really felt it, like I’d finally done something right.

After sharing everything, I paused, then asked the Cameron Hale if there was a secret to being funny—his face scrunched up, thinking hard, and when he finally said 'Silence,' I wasn’t sure if I should laugh or take it seriously.
I walked out on stage with my boom box, the music started, and I just froze—my mouth wouldn’t move, I couldn’t do it, not with them watching me.

I remember Morgan Arden telling me about the sitcom offer. My smile dropped. I said no at first because I hate sitcoms — I told him they're the lowest form of entertainment, with stupid jokes and canned laughter. I wasn't interested in being a comedian on a network show.

After seeing Morgan Arden's reaction, I got up, looked around at all his awards, and then quietly agreed—but only after writing down my terms. I remember clicking the pen shut, handing him the list, and saying 'Those are my terms' with a calm I didn't expect from myself.

I told Morgan Arden to demand Avery Hollis for the show—even if no one knows who he is—because it has to be that way, and I can feel the weight of it in my chest, the silence after, the way they all stared like we were crazy.
I turned around slowly, saw the shock on Morgan Arden's face, and just smiled—then gestured to the empty seat like nothing was wrong. I could see his hands shaking as he tried to make sense of it.

After Morgan Arden started to piece it together, Parker Nolan walked in, and I introduced him like it was all part of the act—I remember the way we both grinned, like we'd just pulled off something brilliant.
I remember locking myself in the dressing room, hearing their voices outside—Judd, Marilu—talking about me like I wasn’t there, like I might not even show up.
I told Parker Nolan I'm gonna quit — the shows are getting worse every time, and I can't stand pretending it matters to me while everyone else celebrates like we're doing something brilliant.

I remember insisting, 'It's my show! Now make it roll!'—and when Blair Vaughn finally agreed to ten seconds, I couldn't help but feel a rush of victory, even though I had to wipe my hand right after shaking his.

When the studio page showed up with that huge mail bag and asked if I wanted my mail, I felt my face light up—I don't even remember smiling that big, but I could feel it, like a spark after all that tension.

I was wiping down tables, sweating, hauling dishes—really doing the work—and when that guy said I looked like Finley Prescott, I just brushed him off. I wanted to be here, in this deli, not back at Silverline Foundation pretending everything was fine.

Morgan Arden showed up and told me to take off the apron, but I yelled back—I’d rather work here than lie for Silverline Foundation. When he mentioned my contract, I finally looked up and said I’d go back, but only as Finley Prescott, not Quinn Brooks. I meant it.

I walked out to applause, smiling and bowing, ready to share something real—songs, puppets, something nice—and then they started shouting that name, 'Quinn Brooks,' over and over, drunk and screaming, until I couldn't pretend I wasn't shaking inside.

I stepped out under the lights and told them I was British—raised in London, educated at Oxford—and that I’d rather do the fine arts than clowning. Then I held up 'The Great Gatsby' and said I’d read it for them, in this clipped accent, like it was the most natural thing in the world.

I was reading quietly, really into it—'vulnerable years,' 'privilege'—when someone suddenly yelled 'Quinn Brooks!!!' and the whole room exploded. I just snapped into him, grinning, 'Tank you veddy much!!!!' and the applause hit me like a wave. Then I went back to the book, like nothing happened.
I slammed the book shut and said I was leaving because they weren't taking me seriously — and then they actually cheered, like they wanted me to go.
I turned back and offered to play a phonograph record instead, thinking they'd reject it — but they roared for it, not realizing it was just the same reading.
I remember mumbling 'I'm sorry, Morgan Arden...' while sitting on the couch, my head down, feeling small as he yelled about the walkouts and the promoter wanting a refund.
I pinned them down, my arms locking them in place, breathing hard—I could feel my heart slamming in my chest—and then I said it: 'You let me win.'
Right after that, I looked at them and asked, 'If I give you three-hundred dollars, will you come to LA and help me destroy a the paper box show?'—just like that, the game switched.

I could hear the weight in Blair Hollis's voice, and when he asked me to agree to fire Finley Prescott, all I could think was how this would destroy him — he's waited his whole life for this. I said yes, but only if they let him down gentle, because I couldn't bear the thought of crushing someone who finally got their chance.
I told Blair Hollis, 'You were brilliant,' and could hear the shock in his breath—like he didn’t know whether to keep raging or believe me.
After saying 'Okay. See you next week,' I hung up, and the silence on the other end felt thick—like the air after a storm passes.
I opened my eyes and told Mom I was fine, then sat up completely deadpan—no flinching, no apology—just calm, like it was nothing.
I sat up and told Mom I was fine, then I was splayed unconscious as they loaded me onto a stretcher amid screaming, flashing cameras, and chaos.

I sat up deadpan after faking the injury, telling Carson Delaney it was just a yoga move—I didn’t feel a thing—and for a second, I felt proud that they’d believed it, that their emotions were real, raw, honest.

When Mom kept crying and hugged me, saying she loved me no matter what, I saw how much I’d scared her—and suddenly, my voice softened, I felt truly sorry, and I told her I shouldn’t have put her through that.
I told them I have cancer, and even after I said it was real—large-celled carcinoma, no less—Morgan Arden still didn’t believe me, not until I looked him dead in the eye and said it again.

memories.memory_text: I walked in just as Morgan Arden realized Finley Prescott was behind the Avery Hollis act, and I could see the shock on his face—he looked like he was about to collapse.
I said 'good show' to Finley Prescott, and he introduced me to Morgan Arden. Finley Prescott and I shared a naughty grin.

Finley Prescott came to me looking defeated again, saying he wanted to quit because each show felt worse to him — I had to snap him out of it by reminding him that 40 million people watching means nothing they think matters, which is exactly why he can use it to screw with them later.
I watched Finley Prescott argue with the technician while I ate my banana, and when he finally got the picture to roll on screen, I almost choked laughing at how pissed Blair Vaughn looked.

I was holding the book, ready to keep things under control, and then Finley Prescott just lunged at me—grabbed it right out of my hands. I flinched, I couldn't help it—he came at me like a damn tornado.
The promoter glared at me like Finley Prescott was some act he could just turn off, but I told him straight—Finley Prescott stops when he says 'The End,' not when some suit gets impatient.

I remember saying it wasn't just bad—it was beyond bad, like we'd stepped into some twisted version of reality nobody could believe, not even me, and Finley Prescott just nodded like he didn't even get it.
Morgan Arden told me to get Finley Prescott to relax, like I’m some kind of caretaker now—me, take him to Hawaii or Bali, find something special. I just stood there, turning it over in my head.
I told Finley Prescott his mother would say 'Now my son is a man,' and after he said it was dirty, I told him the girls clean up between customers. He nodded and said okay.

I saw Morgan Arden double over, then spotted Finley Prescott lying there—Wendy and I ran up, breathless, and in that silent look between us, I knew we were all thinking the same thing: the bit was still on.

I read that paragraph out loud—'Was this in actuality Finley Prescott? And if it was Finley Prescott, is Finley Prescott crazy?'—and the way everyone reacted, you could feel the hoax finally clicking with the public.
I was peeling off that rubber Avery Hollis face in the dressing room, finally stepping out of the shadows — it was mine now, not just a stunt, but my role.
When I said I finally get to be Finley Prescott and dump the water on someone else's head, I could see Morgan Arden was stunned — but I didn’t care, I was fired up.
I dropped to my knees in the Jordan Quincy's gear, watching the tangle of limbs close up, trying to look like I meant it—like any of this was real.
I shoved the Evan Hollis and Cameron Reeves back, then slammed the door and locked it—nobody was getting in unless I said so.
I read that junk about Finley Prescott being rushed to the hospital and faking paralysis, and I couldn't help but laugh—this is exactly what we wanted. It's working for Elvis, I said, and meant it.
When the delivery boy brought the giant flower basket, I saw the card from the the old case crew and thought—this kind of attention is priceless.

I saw Morgan Arden's face when he finally spotted me—his eyes went wide, like he couldn't believe it was me messing with Finley Prescott's set. He looked hurt, confused, like I'd broken some unspoken rule.

I stood up and shouted that Finley Prescott paid me to sabotage him—told the whole room it was a setup, a cheap trick, and that he was creatively dead. I could see the crowd flinch, like they'd been slapped.

I saw the menu and called out the Grand Slam deal—then Finley Prescott drops 'I have cancer' like a lead balloon. I just said, 'Hey, that's good! We can make that play,' and started pitching how we could stretch it out like a fake arc.

After Morgan Arden shot down the idea, I grinned and tossed out that I could push Finley Prescott around in some goofy wheelchair—trying to keep it rolling, but he just shook his head, so I knew he wasn't playing.
Morgan Arden got in my face at Denny's, his voice low and mean, saying if I was behind this he'd kill me — like I'm some puppet master pulling strings for Finley Prescott's bullshit.
I suggested the Santa bit—"Cancer!"—just to cut the bullshit, but Finley Prescott flipped, shouting 'NO NO NO!' like I'd punched him. He wanted it all sparkles and choirs, some flying Santa fantasy.
I stood there with that administrator and said it out loud for the first time — 'The cancer's terminal.' Just like that. Felt the weight of it hit the air.
I told that guy I think crystal healing is horseshit, but if it helps Finley Prescott, then it doesn't matter what I think — and then he told me to leave. Just kicked us out.

I was shoving Finley Prescott’s clothes into the suitcase, hands tight on the fabric, jaw clenched — I couldn’t believe this was falling apart. He just sat there, calm as ever, saying it wasn’t working like it was nothing.

I was holding Finley Prescott's hand, about to shake it like a goodbye — but then I just pulled him into a hug. He looked so sure, so calm, like he was walking into something holy. I don't know what came over me, but for a second, I believed it too.

I saw it — the sack of animal guts slip into Jun's hand under the towel. Then I looked at Finley Prescott's face. The second he realized it was a scam, he didn't get mad. He just started laughing. Not nervous, not bitter — full-on, out-of-his-mind laughing, like it was the funniest thing that ever happened to him.

I stood there watching that filmed Finley Prescott on the screen, smiling like it was all just another bit, singing that damn 'Friendly World' song like we’d rehearsed a hundred times — and I couldn’t tell if I was mourning or managing the punchline.

After the curtain closed and the body disappeared, Reese Prescott and Noel Rivers started whispering — asking if it was wax, if Finley Prescott was coming back — and I just stood there, knowing they still didn’t get it, same as always.

I stood in the shadows watching those kids freak out at the marquee—'Avery Hollis: Live!'—one year to the day after Finley Prescott died, and I couldn't help but smirk. The whole city was losing its mind, screaming, shoving, begging to get in, and I knew it was working exactly as planned.

memories.memory_text: I was on the the blue key with Sammy about a gig when my secretary called out that Avery Hollis was on the line—some associate of Finley Prescott’s—and then this harsh, nasal voice started yelling at me, telling me to stay away from Finley Prescott, that he’d ruin me if I signed him.
I walked into the kitchen, furious, ready to confront Avery Hollis, and then he turned around—it was Finley Prescott, just sitting there like nothing was wrong, smiling like a damn fool.

I saw that rubber face lying next to his plate, and then Parker Nolan shows up, calls Finley Prescott by name, grins like they're in on a joke—turns out his name isn't Gorsky, and he just says 'Don't believe everything you hear' like it's a punchline.

I was shouting at Finley Prescott and Parker Nolan, pacing back and forth, holding that list in my hand — three hundred walkouts, the promoter demanding a refund. I could feel the anger in my voice when I said they don’t mindfuck people in the Midwest like it’s some kind of art.

After yelling, I stopped, lowered my voice, and asked Finley Prescott quietly — really looked at him — and said, 'Who are you trying to entertain? The Parker Quincy... or yourself?' I don’t think he knew the answer, but I needed him to hear it.

I remember standing in the tech booth, watching Finley Prescott strut around the set like he owned it, and telling Blair Hollis, 'But that's Finley Prescott down there. That's not Finley Prescott.' I could feel it — Finley Prescott wasn't present at all.
I called Finley Prescott from the tech booth, put him on speakerphone, and told him Finley Prescott wasn't fitting in—Blair Hollis standing right there, looking nervous as hell.
I was doubled over, trying to catch my breath, and then I saw Finley Prescott lying next to me—just like that, he looked at me and said, 'Hey. Good hustlin','
I was driving down Sunset, minding my own business, when I saw it — the billboard with Finley Prescott and Avery Hollis together, like they were some kind of act, and my stomach just dropped.
I opened the door marked 'Finley Prescott' and saw Finley Prescott inside alone, gathering his things. He looked up, surprised to see me. I didn't go in.
I opened the 'Finley Prescott' door, saw Finley Prescott inside, then went to the 'Avery Hollis' door and opened it.
I walked in and saw Parker Nolan peeling off the Avery Hollis mask, and I couldn't breathe—my chest tightened, I started shaking, like the whole thing was collapsing in on itself.

Finley Prescott kept bouncing, grinning like he'd pulled off something brilliant, and when I said the joke was only funny to him and him alone, it just hung there—empty, like none of it meant anything real anymore.

I remember standing there watching Finley Prescott lift that heavy barbell, the way he just didn't get it — people weren't laughing with him, they were furious, and he kept grinning like it was all going perfectly.

I looked at Finley Prescott eating that cake, so damn cheerful, and I couldn't hold it in anymore — I asked him where that sweet guy went, the one who used to sing Mighty Mouse, and I begged him to stop with the wrestling. It felt like he wasn't even listening.

I told him about the guest-host spot on 'Fridays' — live the paper box, full creative control — a real chance to make people laugh again, but all he latched onto was the word 'live,' like none of the rest even registered.

I heard Finley Prescott yelling about creative control before he stormed off, and I could see the cast muttering, shaking their heads — another mess, another disaster for the reputation I'm trying to fix.
I heard Blair Vaughn scream that he was gonna strangle me—right there in the control booth, after Finley Prescott got cut off on air.
I sat across from Sidney Marlowe, trying to keep my voice steady as I pitched Finley Prescott's apology on Letterman as a real comeback moment—he had to see it as redemption, not just another stunt.
I told Finley Prescott he couldn't work with Adrian Colter anymore — it was the only way to stop the damage, and saying it hurt like hell.
I had to tell Finley Prescott the truth — Westfield Collective didn't want him back, and seeing his face fall like that made it worse.

I called Finley Prescott to tell him the old case was canceled—just said it straight—and he didn’t say a thing. There was this long silence, and when I asked if I should come over, he mumbled something about being busy and hung up.

I was driving down Melrose, just listening to the radio, when I caught sight of the marquee—then I had to look again. It said "Finley Prescott - 9 P.M."... but that can't be right. I thought he was dead.

I was hurrying inside, distracted by comics calling out, but then Micah Vaughn told me Finley Prescott was doing the old material and killing them—then I heard the huge laughter from the showroom, and my eyes widened; something about that sound pulled me in.

I was in the back, watching Finley Prescott struggle on stage, and I could feel something was off — then I saw Parker Nolan shouting over him, throwing off the rhythm, and I thought, 'Who the hell's doing this?' before I realized it was him.

I remember walking with Finley Prescott after the show, both of us just weighed down by how bad it felt. I told him, 'They don't think you suck — they've just lost a reason to love you. You've gotta win back their sympathy.'

I couldn't believe Finley Prescott said he had cancer, and then Parker Nolan started joking about turning it into a bit—I snapped and said it was in terrible taste, that I wanted nothing to do with it.

I looked at that guy saying he was Finley Prescott's therapist and recognized him from 'The In-Laws'—he's an actor, not a real healer. When I called it out, Finley Prescott froze, then started scrambling to explain.

After Finley Prescott broke down, shouting that he was sick and needed support, I asked how I could help—and when he said he wanted to put on the best show ever and reach the top, even Pinecrest Park, I couldn't help but smile gently.

I remember sitting with Finley Prescott as the sun set, feeling his frail hand in mine, and not being able to bring myself to crush his hope when he told me about the psychic surgeon in the Philippines.
I hugged Parker Nolan, and then we stood there whispering—watching everyone look up at that silent film of Finley Prescott smiling down at us, not knowing how to feel, just like always.
